checks.claim: Exact pullback of arbitrary ordered coordinate words, with coordinate labels mapped by the inverse spectator equivalence.
checks.reason: For N=2 the spectator coordinate subtype is exactly three coordinates of i.rev. The reindexing leaves the four KS coordinates fixed and relabels the spectator basis. Both word definitions prepend the outer derivative. The induction maps the entire list without reversing or commuting directions; List.map preserves length. At each step equality is first established on a neighborhood in the open inverse image of the smooth domain, then fderiv_comp applies to the locally smooth tail and the continuous linear inverse. No derivative of the map beyond its fixed linear action, dimension factor, or norm comparison is introduced.
explicit_hypotheses: b real-valued and ContDiffOn real infinity on Omega
inverse image of p belongs to Omega
finite list of canonical coordinate labels
checks.scope_limit: This primitive transports a real smooth coefficient under a linear spectator reindexing. It is not a nonlinear KS change-of-variables theorem or a solution regularity theorem.

checks.claim: D_w(b times fixed complex z) = (D_w b) times z for the displayed real directional derivatives.
checks.reason: Complex-valued derivatives are real Frechet derivatives, matching the real scalar multiplication by b. The base word is definitional equality. The successor step obtains neighborhood equality on the open domain before replacing the global fderiv and uses the local differentiability of the already differentiated real coefficient. Arbitrary constant directions and their order are retained.
explicit_hypotheses: finite spectator type and decidable equality
arbitrary label type and supplied constant direction vectors
checks.scope_limit: A variable amplitude z(p) is not covered; its derivatives would add product terms.

checks.claim: A finite-region coefficient-word bound C yields MemLp 2 and squared-integral budget C^2 * norm(z)^2 * (volume S).toReal for the actual complex source word.
checks.reason: The helper receives the real derivative word as its coefficient and the empty spectator word, so it adds no derivative or spectator-only restriction. Local smoothness gives restricted strong measurability. The explicit finite-measure hypothesis makes the uniform norm bound an L-infinity and then L2 bound. The helper integrates the squared pointwise bound, with the actual region measure rather than a normalized measure. RegionL2Budget includes MemLp 2, preventing a vacuous bound based on Lean nonintegrable-integral defaults. The final almost-everywhere equality has the correct orientation and uses the same restricted volume for both conjuncts.
explicit_hypotheses: S contained in the smooth open Omega
pointwise abs(D_w b) <= C on S
checks.scope_limit: The pointwise coefficient-word bound is an input to this primitive. Its uniform factorial specialization and the identification of a physical source are downstream obligations. The helper parameter _hC is unused, which is harmless redundant data.

checks.claim: The inverse physical spectator reindexing preserves the actual source and target product volumes.
checks.reason: Space and NuclearKSSpace are ordinary products of Euclidean spaces, whose canonical volume instance is the product of factor volumes. The proof applies inner-product-space isometry preservation only to the three-dimensional spectator factor, where its hypotheses apply, then takes the product with the identity measure-preserving map on the four-dimensional KS factor. The ordinary product norm remains the maximum norm. No inner-product instance for that maximum norm or unproved Jacobian normalization is assumed.
explicit_hypotheses: i : Fin 2; all factor measurability, finite-dimensionality and SFinite instances are canonical Euclidean instances
checks.scope_limit: The preserved measure is seven-dimensional KS-coordinate product volume under a linear relabeling, not six-dimensional physical configuration volume under the nonlinear KS lift.

checks.claim: The same real squared-integral budget W and local L2 property transport to a canonical region under inverse reindexing.
checks.reason: The proved image equals preimage identity aligns exactly the two restricted measures. restrict_image_emb applies to any set because the inverse homeomorphism is a measurable embedding, so an additional MeasurableSet O hypothesis is not missing. MemLp composition transfers the first conjunct; the exact integral change-of-variables transfers the second with the same W. For local L2, the inverse sends each compact K to a compact set contained in the physical preimage region before the source local-L2 hypothesis is applied.
